findings.claim_in_draft: A harness that sets only what the model reads (the context, the boundary conditions, the question) replaces nothing. And a harness that partitions a task across calls so that no call sees the others' parts deletes the shared constraints between parts: the whole-explanation results (pairs that pull, the best rival, the same-explanation verdict) fall while the part-by-part marks stand.
findings.finding: M8's two halves cannot both stand. Arm (d) hands each call "only the document, the frozen question and the one test" - entirely a change to what the model reads, so by the first sentence it "replaces nothing", and by the second it deletes shared constraints. The collision is written into the predictions: P2.3 makes "sets only inputs and still shows the loss" the falsifier of M8, and P3.3 predicts exactly that for arm (d). Separately, (F2) will not carry the weight put on it: file 10 states it as a condition a candidate must satisfy, not as a prediction that a partitioned procedure will fail to notice something; the passages that do speak of subset-versus-whole failure are Part VI's. Provenance: built.
findings.evidence: draft P2.3: "If it sets only inputs and still shows the loss, M8 is falsified as written." draft P3.3: "Arm (d) shows fewer same-explanation verdicts and fewer pulling pairs than arm (a) on **more documents than not**". draft arm (d): "fresh calls, one per test of Step 5, each handed only the document, the frozen question and the one test". File 10 Part V: "(F2) prevents a set of locally correct pieces from hiding a lost shared constraint." File 10 Part VI: "A block may be critical while no singleton in it is." and "**Interference.** \(\Gamma=\{a,b\}\), \(\mathsf S=\{\{a\}\}\): the full candidate fails although a subset succeeds. Success of a subset does not imply success of the whole; \(b\) is not made "not a commitment" to repair this."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a place where the draft distinguishes two losses - the owner's capability loss of Q1 from the loss of cross-step fields - which would let P2.3 and P3.3 speak about different things. I read M8, Q1, P2.3, P3.3 and section 8's bullet "P3.2 or P3.3 fail in the direction 'no drop'": one phrase, "the loss", carries both and nothing separates them. I also looked for a sentence of file 10 turning (F2) into a claim about procedures; Part V states it only as what (F2) prevents in a candidate.
findings.forced_edit: Split the two losses: a component replaced (Part II's "An edit that sets a port replaces the component assigning that port") from a context or contract narrowed (Part VI's critical block and interference). Restate P2.3's falsifier for the first only, and re-anchor the partition claim to Part VI, not to (F2).

findings.where: M3, section 3 ("Why phase 3 is the first test"), M5 (i), P3.1, trap 4 (question 4, fault shape)
findings.claim_in_draft: Nothing about what an agent instantiates is read off one report; it is read off what changes between reports under admitted changes.
findings.finding: Derivation 9 is a limit on what input-output behaviour can settle, and the draft cites it as the licence for settling it that way - the same shape of fault the H68 scout found in the word list's reading of (K3). The theorem's two systems share the whole input-output projection, which is precisely "what changes between reports under admitted changes" to the input, and it says no function of that projection decides an account claim. So it licenses the predictions of difference (P3.2, P3.3, P3.4) and forbids the inference M5 (i) and P3.1 invite: that agreement on every field shows the two arrangements instantiate the same thing. The draft's own trap says as much, and a prediction of no change is evidence of nothing by that rule. The holder for the weaker claim the draft could make is Derivation 2's consequence and (K), which the draft never cites anywhere. Provenance: built.
findings.evidence: File 10 Derivation 9: "**Claim.** If \(M_0,M_1\) have the same input-output projection and differ on an account claim, no function of the projection agrees with the claim on both." File 10 Part 0: "Two systems with identical outputs and different internal routes are different organizations here, and the semantics says so." File 10 Derivation 2: "**Consequence.** Underdetermination of an account by a contract is not a failure of the semantics to decide; it is the semantics reporting that the contract does not contain the distinction. ... A claim that two such candidates "really" differ is a claim that some admitted change separates them, and must supply it." draft M5: "(i) a fresh call handed the whole transcript instantiates, at the grain of text, what the stateful agent instantiates, and the two will not differ on any field". draft trap: "**Reading a reader's report as what the reader instantiates.** Derivation 9 forbids it; only what changes between arms is evidence."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for anything in file 10 licensing the agreement direction - a passage saying indistinguishability under a contract establishes sameness of what is instantiated. Derivation 2 comes closest, requires both candidates already to satisfy (F1), (F2) and (A) on C, and delivers only "one account at grain \(C\)", not sameness of instantiation. Part 0 grants that a difference in outputs shows a difference and denies the converse. I also checked by grep that the draft never cites Derivation 2: only 3, 5 and 9 appear.
findings.forced_edit: Restate M5 (i) as "no admitted change on this contract separates them - one account at grain \(C\)", citing Derivation 2's consequence and (K); add to P3.1 that agreement settles nothing about what is instantiated. Keep the prediction of non-difference, which is testable; drop the instantiation claim its success would not license.

findings.claim_in_draft: A judge showing that the programme's use of file 10 rests on one of the theory's own attack points (Part 0, A to E) as if it were settled. The model must not assume sufficiency (A) or that any agent belongs to a class (Part 0's "does not prove").
findings.finding: The draft's own failure condition is met twice by the draft. M2's load-bearing consequence rests on Derivation 3, which is the first limb of attack point (D) and a named defeat condition in Part XV; M8's answer to Q1 is an eliminative explanation - why there is no whole-explanation result under the partition - whose treatment file 10 marks as possibly inadequate under attack (B). Neither is named as an attack point anywhere in the draft; section 9 names only (A) and class membership, and M2's "would count against it" raises only the blindness question. The class-membership half I could not catch out: "What the model does not claim" quotes Part 0 exactly and no phase attributes a class. Provenance: built.
findings.evidence: File 10 Part 0: "**(D) Genesis.** Show either that a selected transport can be non-underdetermined on unseen changes (against Derivation 3), or that construction reduces to selection (against Part IV), or that the primitive layer described in Part IV is not in fact what explanation operates on." and "**(B) Necessity.** ... Explanations that work by showing a supposed structure is absent are the hard case; Part VII gives the semantics' treatment, and it may be inadequate." File 10 Part VII: "This is the semantics' treatment of eliminative explanation; it is offered as adequate and is listed under attack (B) as a place where it may not be." File 10 Part XV: "**A non-fallible selected transport.** A selection history \(H\subsetneq C\) whose survivor is determined on \(C\setminus H\). This refutes Derivation 3." HV word-list.md Traps: "The source marks its own weak points (Part 0, "Where to attack this", and Part XV). The treatment of absences is one. Pass that caution on when it applies."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for the draft naming (B) or (D), or passing on file 10's caution about absences. Grepping the draft for "attack", "Part 0", "Part XV", "eliminative" and "absence": section 9's bullet is the only mention of the attack points and names (A) and class membership only; Part XV is never cited; the absence caution appears nowhere, though trap 7 does pass on Part XIII's barrier caution.
findings.forced_edit: Name (D) beside M2 and (B) beside M8, each with file 10's own caution quoted, and say what the programme does if either attack succeeds - since M2 and M8 carry the answers to Q1, Q2 and Q4.

findings.claim_in_draft: Training fits every clause: the population is the parameter settings reached, \(\mu\) the update, \(H\) the training history, survival the loss condition, and nothing in the training data represents the model or the loss.
findings.finding: The clause the draft itself picks out as the one to watch is asserted, not shown, and the gloss drops one of its three limbs: file 10 forbids the history from representing \(t\), \(H\), or the survival condition, and the draft addresses \(t\) and the survival condition only. For a reader whose corpus contains machine-learning writing - which the draft's own readers under test are - occurrences in that history plausibly do represent the survival condition, and "represents" in file 10 is satisfied by any faithful transport with constructed provenance, which a correct description of a loss function has. Worse, two clauses pull against each other: whatever makes the survival condition "enacted by the environment" in Part XII's sense (the training loop and its loss code) is itself a member of the physical history that represents the survival condition. Under the skill's rule that "found nowhere" means unknown, the fit of this clause is unknown and M2's own falsifier is live. The population limb I do not press: a serial reading (the settings actually visited) makes it arguable. Provenance: asserted.
findings.evidence: File 10 Part IV: "No member of the history represents \(t\), \(H\), or the survival condition." File 10 Part XII: "A selected provenance \(\operatorname{Sel}(t;\mathcal T,\mu,H)\) is a claim about a physical history: a population of realized transports, a physically admitted variation operator, and a survival condition enacted by the environment. It is fallible and checkable as any physical claim is." File 10 (R): "admits a transport to \(c\) that is faithful on \(c\)'s contract and whose provenance is selected or constructed". File 10 Part IV: "Construction is not selection. A selected transport has no represented target in its history; a constructed one does." HV testing-against-cases.md: "**"Found nowhere" means unknown.** It shows neither "unneeded" nor "impossible". "I did not find X" describes your search." draft M2 falsifier: "a judge showing that a training update fails one of the four formal clauses".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a sentence restricting "represents" in that clause to representations owned by the system whose transport it is, which would let a third party's description of the loss sit harmlessly in the history. Only Part X's Build carries ownership ("an actual subhistory owned by \(s\)"); the Selected clause's no-representation sentence carries no ownership qualifier, and Part XII repeats that the whole thing is "a claim about a physical history", checkable as any physical claim is. I also checked whether "blind" occurs anywhere but Part 0, in case the formal clause imported it: one hit, Part 0.
findings.forced_edit: Mark clause 4's fit as unknown and name the check that would settle it - whether any occurrence in a reader's selection history represents \(t\), \(H\) or the survival condition - or drop "fits every clause" and say which clauses are shown. Add the missing limb \(H\) to the gloss.

findings.where: M1 and section 1, bearing on M4, M5 and M8
findings.claim_in_draft: What organization the execution instantiates, \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell\), is the physical module's and is not claimed here.
findings.finding: Two things, both about the one input the semantics takes from outside. First, section 1's quotation does not do the job given it: the sentence puts \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell\) outside at every grain, the grain of text included, so it does not single out the weights; the nearer passage for choosing a grain is Part XIV's "Indices, not primitives", which the draft never cites. Second, (R) cannot be applied without \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell\), and M1 declines to supply it while M4 applies (R) to a reader's report organization at the grain of text, M5 (i) claims two arrangements instantiate the same organization at that grain, and M8 claims components are deleted. File 10 makes supplying it a condition of membership, so M4's own falsifier - that (R) cannot be applied to a report organization at the grain of text at all - is triggered not by the theory but by M1. M1's provenance: asserted; the parts resting on it are held only if it supplies what it declines to.
findings.evidence: File 10 Part IV: "The one thing (R) takes from outside is \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell(o)\): which organization a physical occurrence instantiates at a grain. That is supplied by the physical module, not by the semantics." File 10 Part XIV: "**Indices, not primitives.** Grain \(\ell\), boundary \(\beta\), continuity \(\Omega\), and the contract \(C\) are declared indices. Every claim is relative to them; none is a predicate that could be true or false." File 10 Part XIV: "**Membership.** The base class: interpretations supplying these data with correct typing, satisfying physical realization wherever a physical attribution is made." File 10 Part I: "Every attribution of an organization to a physical system must be permitted by the adopted physics." File 10 Derivation 6: "**Claim.** Every predicate in Parts II-XIII is defined from \(\Theta\) (including \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell\)) and, where invoked, \(\mathcal N\), together with declared indices." draft M4 falsifier: "a judge showing that (R) cannot be applied to a reader's report organization at the grain of text at all".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for file 10 allowing \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell\) to be left open, or for a form of (R) that does not need it. Derivation 6 and Part XIV's primitives paragraph both make it required data of any interpretation, and (R)'s own text names it as the one external input. I also checked that section 10 frames the choice correctly ("outside the programme by choice"), which cures the framing but not the missing supply.
findings.forced_edit: In M1, declare \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell\) at the grain of text - what organization a call's carrier text instantiates - as the model's declared physical input, marked declared, rather than declining to claim it; and re-anchor section 1's grain choice to "Indices, not primitives".

findings.where: section 4, "What the model does not claim"
findings.claim_in_draft: That an agent is creative, understands, or knows: those are (G), Deploy and (EK), each of which needs a construction witness and an owned history, and phase 1 does not attribute them.
findings.finding: Deploy needs neither. It needs a representation by (R), whose provenance may be selected, integrated into problem-directed activity and held as a retained capability; the dependence order puts Deploy on (R) and (CT1) while Build is a separate branch. As written the sentence would make understanding on selected provenance impossible, which is the opposite of what file 10 allows. (G) and (EK) do need a witness and an owned history. Provenance: built.
findings.evidence: File 10 Part X: "**Deployment.** \(\operatorname{Deploy}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,\xi;U)\) holds when \(s\) at \(\xi\) holds a representation of \(c\) - by (R), a faithful transport with selected or constructed provenance - integrated into problem-directed activity and supporting the declared use task \(U\) as a retained capability (Part XII). ... A system may understand a false theory." File 10 Part XIV: "Deploy depends on (R) and (CT1). Build depends on histories and (E)."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a clause of Deploy or of the dependence order requiring construction. The Deployment paragraph names (R) and retention only; the dependence order separates Deploy from Build. (EK) does route through Origin and so through Build, and (G) is "Attempt \(\land\) New \(\land\) Build", so the claim holds for those two.
findings.forced_edit: "(G) and (EK) need a construction witness and an owned history; Deploy needs a representation by (R) - selected provenance suffices - and a retained capability (CT1)."

findings.claim_in_draft: It is **a construction** when the theory permits the object (as Derivation 5 permits a contract to be an organization) but does not contain it, and it is marked so.
findings.finding: The one example the draft gives of its third mark is an example of its first. Derivation 5 does not merely permit a contract to be an organization; its claim sentence asserts it and its proof establishes it, so the object is contained in file 10. The H68 scout uses Derivation 5 the other way round - as what permits a further construction the theory does not contain. Provenance: built.
findings.evidence: File 10 Derivation 5: "**Claim.** A contract \(C\) is an organization (a set of edits with a query), and can be the content \(c\) in (G)." scout_word-list-vs-file-10.json, row "a held limit carries its reason inside the explanation": "The theory does permit the construction - Derivation 5 makes a contract an organization with "admitted edits (add or remove a change; alter \(\mathcal Q\))" - but Part VIII then makes each such edit a new index rather than a variation inside one frozen assessment."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for Derivation 5 being stated as a permission rather than a claim. Its proof reads as a recipe - "Give it ports (the edits and their boundaries), components (the closure conditions), and admitted edits ... It is then a \(D\) in the sense of (O)" - which is the rival reading and the reason I press this no further than the illustration; but the claim sentence is a flat assertion, so as an example of "permits but does not contain" it fails.
findings.forced_edit: Replace the example with an object file 10 does not contain - the scout's "hard-to-vary over scope: Pres(F) under edits to the contract", or the draft's own M5 reading of CT2.

findings.claim_in_draft: **M2. The weights are a selected transport.**
findings.finding: A transport in file 10 runs between two organizations and has no components of its own; components belong to organizations. The weights sit on the occurrence side of (R): the organization they instantiate at a grain is what admits a transport. M8 compounds the slide with "the selected transport's own components", an object file 10 does not have - and M8's whole deletion argument needs components, so it needs the organization, not the transport. M4 gets the same relation right for a reader's report. Provenance: built.
findings.evidence: File 10 Part IV: "A transport from an organization \(D\) to an organization \(E\) is \[t=(\pi,\tau,\sigma,\lambda)\] where \(\pi:X_D\to X_E\) on the stated scope, \(\tau\) translates edits, \(\sigma\) translates boundaries, and \(\lambda\) assigns each component of \(E\) a subnetwork of \(D\) with a port translation." File 10 Part II: "\(J\) indexes components; each component \(j\) has a footprint \(V_j\subseteq V\)." File 10 (R): "An occurrence \(o\) **represents** content \(c\) at grain \(\ell\) when the organization that \(o\) instantiates under the physical module, at grain \(\ell\), admits a transport to \(c\)". draft M8: "sets ports that the selected transport's own components assign".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a sentence giving a transport components or ports of its own, or calling a carrier a transport. Part IV's tuple gives \(\lambda\) the job of assigning components of \(E\) subnetworks of \(D\); Part II gives components only to organizations; Part XII's selection paragraph speaks of "a population of realized transports" between organizations of a physical system, never of a carrier being one.
findings.forced_edit: "The organization the weights instantiate at the grain of text admits a selected transport", and in M8 "the components of that organization" rather than the transport's.

findings.claim_in_draft: The formal definition needs no blindness and Derivation 3's proof uses none, so M2 rests on the formal definition and says so.
findings.finding: Held on blindness: I read Derivation 3's proof and it uses none, and "blind" occurs in file 10 only in Part 0. But the proof does use a premise M2 never names - that the component relations are supplied independently for each edit-boundary pair - and a parametric family with tied weights is exactly the shape file 10 names as what would refute Derivation 3. M2's consequence, on which the draft's licence to call a reader "unconstrained" off its history depends, is held only if that premise holds of a neural network. Setting blindness aside also buys less than it looks: Part IV's own no-representation clause does the work blindness did, and that is the clause M2 asserts without evidence. Provenance: built.
findings.evidence: File 10 Derivation 3 proof: "The component relations \(L_j(a,b)\) are supplied independently for each \((a,b)\). Survival on \(H\) constrains only \(\{L_j(a,b):(a,b)\in H\}\). Alter \(L_{j}(a,b)\) for one \((a,b)\notin H\) to any other admitted relation; the result survives on \(H\) and differs at \((a,b)\)." File 10 Part XV: "**A non-fallible selected transport.** A selection history \(H\subsetneq C\) whose survivor is determined on \(C\setminus H\). This refutes Derivation 3." File 10 Part 0: "A correspondence can be *selected* - produced by blind variation and survival on a history of predictions". File 10 Part IV: "a selected transport has no represented target and no criticism in its history; a constructed one has both."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for blindness in the proof, and for independence being derived rather than assumed. The proof's first sentence states independence as a supplied fact about \(L\); nothing in it mentions how the survivor was produced. I also checked that the population in Derivation 3 is unrestricted - the claim says "there exists a transport \(t'\)", not "a member of \(\mathcal T\)" - which is what makes a restricted population the live counterexample.
findings.forced_edit: Add to M2's "would count against it": a judge showing a reader's transport family violates "supplied independently for each \((a,b)\)", that is, that survival on \(H\) does constrain behaviour off \(H\); and say that Part IV's no-representation clause, not blindness, is what M2 must establish.

findings.where: M8 (question 2, first half), with sections 1, 10 and 11
findings.claim_in_draft: The loss tracks *which* ports are set (the outputs of the model's components: what to attend to, what to emit next), not *how much* is set.
findings.finding: Setting a token is within the theory's admitted edits and is exactly what Part II's quoted sentence describes, so the token half is held. "What to attend to" is not a port at the grain the plan declares. The programme works "at the grain of text", section 10 puts \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell\) of a transformer outside by choice and section 11 excludes weights and activations, so at the declared grain M8's answer to Q1 shrinks to "a harness that writes the tokens replaces the emission component", and the attention half - the owner's actual difficulty - has no grain in this programme to live at. Neither of M8's falsifiers reaches it. Provenance: built.
findings.evidence: draft section 1: "This programme works at the grain of text: what is in the context, what is emitted, and what changes in the emission when the context is changed." draft section 10: "**The grain is text.** \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell\) of a transformer is outside the programme by choice (section 1)." draft section 11: "Anything at the grain of weights or activations." File 10 Part II: "A port \(v\) is an **input** under \(A\) when \(A\) contains an edit that sets \(v\) directly." and "An edit that sets a port replaces the component assigning that port; it does not add an equation beside an incompatible one."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a reading on which attention is a text-grain port. Choosing which context slices a call reads is attention in a loose sense and is a text-grain edit - but M8 files that under what the model reads, the harmless kind. So the damaging kind sits at the excluded grain, and the rescue collapses M8's own distinction rather than saving it.
findings.forced_edit: Say that Q1's attention half falls outside the declared grain: either declare a coarse attention port at the grain of text (which slices of the record a call is given) and keep the claim there, or record Q1 as only partly reachable under P1.2.

findings.claim_in_draft: Part XII: "**Owned capability.** \(\operatorname{Can}_{\Omega,\beta}(\xi,T;\chi)\) requires an owned retained realization or an owned, physically admitted, finite construction of one under the same continuity and resource contract. A theorist's description of a protocol is not the system's possession of it."
findings.finding: The quotation is exact and the use of its last sentence against label-reading is held. But every ownership predicate the draft leans on is indexed to a boundary and a continuity the draft never declares: Can carries \(\Omega,\beta\), Deploy and Build carry \(\beta,\ell\). M5's stateful/stateless distinction is a continuity question; M9's "scrutinizable by the agent ... only by its designer" is a boundary question; M4's and M6's owned subhistory is both. File 10 says every claim is relative to these declared indices. In the draft the words "boundary" and "continuity" appear only inside quotations and in "boundary conditions". Provenance: built.
findings.evidence: File 10 Part XII: "\(\operatorname{Can}_{\Omega,\beta}(\xi,T;\chi)\)"; Part X: "\(\operatorname{Deploy}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,\xi;U)\)" and "\(\operatorname{Build}_{\beta,\ell}(s,c,h,e)\)". File 10 Part XIV: "Grain \(\ell\), boundary \(\beta\), continuity \(\Omega\), and the contract \(C\) are declared indices. Every claim is relative to them; none is a predicate that could be true or false."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I grepped the draft for "boundary", "continuity", "index" and "indices". The hits are the Selected clause's "edit-boundary pairs", M6's and M8's "boundary conditions", the Can quotation's "continuity and resource contract", and "index" only where the draft means the contract index (M10, section 6). Neither \(\beta\) nor \(\Omega\) is declared anywhere.
findings.forced_edit: Declare \(\beta\) (does the system include the harness, the record, the owner?) and \(\Omega\) before M4, M5, M6 and M9 use predicates carrying them; M9's stronger claim - that a harness policy is scrutinizable only by its designer - is a claim about where \(\beta\) is drawn and cannot stand without it.

findings.where: P1.3, P1.4, section 6 (Part VI row), section 1 (the eleven left_out notions)
findings.claim_in_draft: **P1.3.** Of the eleven notions of file 10 that the HV word list uses without a row (H69), the model's word list carries a row for **at least six** and names the rest as not needed by the model, with the reason.
findings.finding: The count and the description are exact: the scout's left_out list has eleven entries, each naming where the skill uses the notion with no row. The draft uses three of them and uses none of them wrongly that I could find - obligations and protected obligations (M10, correctly credited as notion 2), "Losses outside \(P\) must be exposed" (M10), explanatory realism (section 10). But two the draft's own claims need are absent, and P1.3's "at least six" does not require either. Item 4, the finite monotone theorem with its unassumed condition, is the theory's ground for the marks *held* and *idle* and for removing in groups - exactly what P1.4 predicts over - and section 6's Part VI row writes "none named" in its Gap column where that condition is a gap. Item 8, grain as a declared index, is the passage section 1's grain choice and M5 (i)'s "at the grain of text" need, and the one section 1 should have cited. Provenance of the sketch's word-list claims: built; of M10's mappings: fitted.
findings.evidence: scout_word-list-vs-file-10.json left_out item 4: "This is the theory's statement of exactly when removing one part at a time settles anything, and its own note that the condition is not assumed in general. No row states the theorem, the condition, or "critical singleton" and "globally indispensable" - which are the theory's words for *held*, the skill's commonest mark." File 10 Part VI: "**Finite monotone theorem.** If \(\Gamma\) is finite, \(\mathsf S\) is upward closed, and \(\Gamma\in\mathsf S\), then the critical singletons are exactly \(\bigcup\min\mathsf S\) and the globally indispensable ones are exactly \(\bigcap\min\mathsf S\)." and "No upward closure and no minimal member are assumed." left_out item 8: "File 10 uses grain in two senses, the physical \(\ell\) of \(\operatorname{Org}_\ell\) and "one account at grain \(C\)" in Derivation 2, which is the contract; the skill's "level" is the second." draft P1.4: "leave **no part idle** and **at most two parts loose**". draft section 6: "| Support, critical blocks, redundant routes, interference, Pres(F) (Part VI) | (S), (B), (D) | HV file 33, Step 5 (remove in groups, two routes, pull) and the eight marks | none named |"
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for the draft naming either notion: grep for "monotone", "upward", "critical", "singleton", "indispensable", "Indices" found nothing. I also checked whether the draft uses any of the eleven wrongly, reading each of its three uses against its file 10 sentence, and found only the narrower reading of *fixed*, reported separately, not a misuse.
findings.forced_edit: Name items 4 and 8 in P1.3 as required rather than optional, and change section 6's Part VI Gap from "none named" to the finite monotone theorem's condition, which is what decides when P1.4's marks *held* and *idle* mean anything.

findings.claim_in_draft: So the part of the reasoning architecture the context must consume is exactly: the frozen question with its change list, the parts of the explanation under test, and any target a construction at this call is to bind to.
findings.finding: Only the third item is held by the passages quoted. Part IV requires a represented target for a constructed transport and locates the requirement in an episode; Part X locates it over "an actual subhistory owned by \(s\)" - a history, not one execution - so "at this call" tightens an episode-level condition into a per-call one with no passage behind it. Part III's tuple is a fact about what a question is, not a requirement that an execution's readable occurrences contain \(C\), \(b_0\) and \(O_p\). P3.4, which tests only rivals and pulling pairs, tests the third item alone, so "exactly" reaches further than the plan's own test. The catch-all in the same part ("Everything else ... may sit outside") does carry a gauge: the tool audit. Provenance: built.
findings.evidence: File 10 Part IV: "**Constructed.** There is an episode (Part X) whose construction witness prepares \(t\), and in which \(t\), or the organization it targets, is available as a represented target." File 10 Part X: "holds when an actual subhistory owned by \(s\) and delimited at \(e\) prepares a represented organization for explanatory use of \(c\)". File 10 Part III: "\(O_p\) is the set of obligations being addressed or protected." draft P3.4: "In **zero** runs does a reader name a rival or a pulling pair whose target was not in its context and not in any file its tool audit shows it read."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for a passage requiring a question's parts to be represented at each execution. Part III makes the question a tuple; the only per-event indices in file 10 are the \(\xi\) of Deploy, Can and scrutinizability, which are about retention and continuation, not about what a call's context contains.
findings.forced_edit: Restrict "exactly" to the construction target and mark the frozen question and the parts under test as the plan's own requirement (a construction); or index M6 to the owned subhistory and say what makes one call the whole of it.

findings.where: M7 and M10 (question 4, second fault shape)
findings.claim_in_draft: The record of this repository is such a memory: "A history \(h\) is a set of occurrences with an acyclic causal precedence \(\prec_h\)" (Part IX)
findings.finding: The quotation stops one clause short of the definition's end, and the omitted clause is the hardest for a folder of files to meet. M7's falsifier list omits it too, naming only acyclicity and leaves-referring-to-events, so no judge following that list could catch it. The same truncation carries into M10's "The log is a history with precedence (Part IX)", and M10's "results files are evidence leaves" reads a whole file as a leaf where a leaf is a reference to one event - the whole-for-part widening the H68 scout caught twice elsewhere in the word list. Provenance of M10's mappings: fitted (written with the existing conventions in view, and its falsifier only ever tests the fit it was made from).
findings.evidence: File 10 Part IX: "**Histories.** A history \(h\) is a set of occurrences with an acyclic causal precedence \(\prec_h\) and a physical interpretation supplying process occurrences, their ports, and the connections actually instantiated." and "An evidence leaf is a reference to an event with an interpreted claim. A receipt is a derivation tree over leaves." draft M7 falsifier: "(for instance, that its precedence is not acyclic, or that its leaves do not refer to events)". draft M10: "The log is a history with precedence (Part IX); results files are evidence leaves".
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for the omitted clause being decorative, or for the record supplying it. Part IX's next definition leans on the same interpretation - "An **active route** is a connected subnetwork of actual occurrences joining a represented input to an operative result, whose components satisfy the applicable relations" - so the clause is load-bearing. The nearest thing the record holds is the tool audits of H61 and H68, which the draft cites elsewhere but not here.
findings.forced_edit: Quote the clause in full; add to M7's falsifier "or that no physical interpretation supplies the ports and the connections actually instantiated"; and say that entries in results files, not the files, are the evidence leaves.

findings.claim_in_draft: A stateful agent is one whose executions return into a state that carries the represented targets of its unfinished work (the retention fixed point, CT2)
findings.finding: CT2 says which states have executions that complete and return into \(C\), and that \(F\) is monotone with a greatest fixed point. It says nothing about what those states carry. Defining \(C\) as the states carrying represented targets is permitted - an attribute is a set of a substrate's states - but it is the draft's object, not CT2's, and it is not marked as a construction, against the draft's own rule at the top. It is load-bearing: the whole stateful/stateless distinction, and so M5, P3.1 and P3.2, rest on it. Provenance: built.
findings.evidence: File 10 Part XII: "**Retention fixed point.** \(F(C)\) = states whose executions all complete and return into \(C\). \(F\) is monotone; \(C\subseteq F(C)\) is the invariant form; the union of post-fixed sets is the greatest fixed point. (CT2)" and "A substrate is a physical system; an attribute a set of its states; a task a permitted input-to-output attribute transformation with explicit resources and side effects." draft, section 4 preamble: "where the plan builds something the theory permits but does not contain, it says so."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I read Part XII in full looking for anything constraining what a retained state carries: CT1 constrains completion and return into \(C\), CT2 the fixed-point structure, Can the ownership; none constrains \(C\)'s contents beyond its being an attribute.
findings.forced_edit: Mark it as a construction and name the permitting sentences (an attribute is a set of states; CT2's \(C\)), as M1 and section 7 do elsewhere.

findings.where: section 9, first bullet, bearing on M1, M4 and M7
findings.claim_in_draft: A phase 1 model whose every part is a frame (declared) and none a claim: the theory forbids resting on it, and the programme would be describing, not explaining.
findings.finding: The theory's restriction is not about proportions of frames to claims; it forbids any claim about creativity resting on declaration, claim by claim. A model with nine claims and one frame would pass the draft's test and still break the rule, which is the live case here: M1 is the declared frame, and M4's relay-is-not-construction claim and M7's declared-versus-constructed retrieval distinction are claims about construction that rest on it. The falsifier as written is the wrong shape to catch that. Provenance: built.
findings.evidence: File 10 Part 0: "Declaration is permitted only as a modelling convenience, and a claim about creativity cannot rest on it." File 10 Part IV: "A declared transport does not make an occurrence represent anything; it makes a modeller assert that it does." draft M1: "(Declared frame.)" draft M7: "A lookup the designer wrote is declared; a query the agent built from a represented difficulty is constructed."
findings.what_would_show_wrong: I looked for file 10 putting the restriction at the level of a model rather than a claim. Part 0's provenance paragraph and Part IV's Declared clause are both per-transport and per-claim; nothing counts frames.
findings.forced_edit: Restate the failure condition as "any claim of the model about construction or creativity that rests on the declared frame", and check M4 and M7 against it before phase 1 freezes.

findings.where: section 6 (the whole table), against the draft's own rule in its opening

Twelve of its thirteen rows name theory terms - "(Q), contract", "(S), (B), (D)", "receipts, \(h\)", "(CT1), (CT2), Can", "(K), rule signature", "\(\mathcal N\)" - with only a Part number beside them; the dependence order is the section's only quotation. findings.claim_in_draft: a job tagged *fixed* is a protected obligation ("protected obligations \(P\), fixed for the comparison", Part XI), which is the row the HV word list lacked (H69's unmapped notion 2)

But the nearer half of the draft's own quotation is "fixed for the comparison". A protected obligation is checked for preservation - (P) has \(\forall r\in P[r(\xi)\Rightarrow r(\xi')]\) as a conjunct - while an HV job tagged *fixed* is one no test is run on at all. The "must" is not held: (RC) is a class condition, not a requirement file 10 places on anyone, and the theory says it supplies no merit function and does not derive the normative relation. It supplies places where such things would go if anyone had them, and marks those places as empty." verdict:
1. THE QUESTION, FROZEN. What: whether each sentence of the draft that uses or quotes a term of file 10 is held, loose, a construction or a contradiction by the draft's own section 7 definitions, read no wider than written. Over what range: draft sections 1, 3, 4 (M1-M10), 6, 7, 9, 10, against file 10 alone, plus the H68 scout JSON for the two MISMATCH rows and the eleven left_out entries. What is asked: a rule-status question (what counts as what under section 7's rule and the skill's eight marks), not a production question about whether the model is true or the phases will work. Not asked and not answered: whether the model is right, whether the phases are runnable, the record claims beyond two spot checks, and the other judges' remits.

2. THE PARTS AND THE JOBS. Parts, in the draft's own numbering: M1 to M10; section 5's predictions where they carry a theory term (P1.1-P1.4, P2.3, P3.1-P3.4); section 6's thirteen-row table and its dependence-order quotation; section 7's four definitions; section 9's four failure conditions; section 10's five weaknesses. Jobs: J1 given - every claim using a theory term quotes the sentence it rests on (the draft's opening). J2 given - where the plan builds what the theory permits but does not contain, it says so (same sentence). J3 given - each of Q1 to Q6 gets a statement whose falsifier is a run this repository can make (P1.2). J4 given - no part rests on an attack point as settled (section 9). J5 fixed - file 10 is the only authority (S4); not up for test here. J6 added, mine - every quoted passage is read no wider than written and at the Part the draft names. J7 added, mine - every index file 10 declares (grain, boundary, continuity, contract) is declared before a predicate carrying it is used. Parts held only by J6 or J7 are marked "held if" and say so.

3. PART BY PART, with provenance beside each mark. M1: fixed (the draft put it outside test and said so), provenance asserted - and load-bearing for M4, M5 and M8, which are held only if M1 supplies the Org_l it declines to claim. M2: held if, provenance built - the Part IV quotation is exact and the blindness point is correct, but clause 4's fit is unknown and Derivation 3's independence premise is unnamed; its headline sentence ("the weights are a selected transport") is loose against Part IV's transport tuple. M3: split - held for "never read off its emission" (Derivation 9 plus "Occurrences are not identified by carrying the same words"), contradicts for "it is read off what changes"; provenance built. M4: held if (needs M1's Org_l), with one loose citation (the relay sentence anchors construction, not representation); provenance built. M5: held if, provenance built - beta and Omega undeclared, the CT2 gloss an unmarked construction, and (i)'s instantiation claim unlicensed by the theorem cited. M6: loose, provenance built - only the construction-target item is held; its catch-all ("Everything else ... may sit outside") does carry a gauge, the tool audit. M7: split - held for "A declared transport does not make an occurrence represent anything", loose for the record-as-history on a truncated definition; provenance built. M8: contradicts, provenance built - its two halves cannot both stand, and its attention half has no grain at the declared grain. M9: held for "an attention policy" being an aspect of practice (verbatim in Part I), held if for the "must"; provenance built. M10: mixed, provenance fitted - held for the declared contract and obligations, the assessment at a fixed index, the historical index and "Losses outside P must be exposed"; loose for log-as-history, results-files-as-leaves, and "protected" where "fixed for the comparison" is nearer. Section 7's four definitions: held, held, contradicts on its illustration of "construction", held. Section 9: bullet 1 loose (misreads the declaration restriction), bullet 4 contradicts (its own condition is met by M2 and M8), bullets 2 and 3 untested here. Section 10: held - the Part I quotation is exact and the weaknesses it names are real; the second bullet's "by choice" is the right word and does not cure what M1 withholds. No totals: one part, M8, carries the answers to Q1, Q2 and Q4, and its failure costs more than the held rows earn.

4. WHOLE-EXPLANATION CHECKS, every test named. Remove: bit - cutting the dependence-order citation from section 3 costs nothing (idle). Swap: bit - swapping M5's cited Part for M6's, and M10's "protected" for "fixed for the comparison", both survive and name nearer passages. Poke: bit - the change that should matter is handing arm (d) only inputs, and M8 says both that this replaces nothing and that it deletes shared constraints. Flip the outcome: COULD NOT BITE on M2, M3 and section 7, because their content is derived - Derivations 3, 9 and 5 are theorems of file 10, and file 33 says flip is "Not for a derived conclusion". Substituted the proofs test, drop a condition, which produced the finding about Derivation 3's independence premise. Reverse: COULD NOT BITE. The sentence that leaves it nothing to reach is the research question itself, "Which of the theory's objects does an agent built on a large language model instantiate at one call, which across calls, ... and which never" - an identification and rule-status query, not a production claim, so there is no cause to poke at one end and effect at the other. The part it would have settled, whether the arrangement produces the field loss or the field loss identifies the arrangement, is left UNKNOWN, and phase 3's arms are the test that would settle it. Hunt the answer in the starting points: bit - section 3 puts the test design ("only what changes between arms is evidence") in at the start and then cites Derivation 9 as the theory's rule for it, when Derivation 9 is the limit on that very move. Add a job: bit twice - J6 and J7 produced the Org_l and the beta/Omega findings, and both ruled out the reading of M4, M5 and M9 on which they need no declaration. Build the best rival: bit - the rival is that an LLM's weights carry a transport with CONSTRUCTED provenance operating on selected material, since the loss and the target behaviours are represented in the training history by their designers; the change that tells it from M2 is whether any occurrence in that history represents t, H or the survival condition, which is inspectable, and M2 asserts the answer instead of testing it. Pull: bit twice - M8's input-only-is-harmless against partition-loses-jobs (the taxonomy "which ports, not how much" gives way, and the line is whether restricting a context counts as setting a port); and in M2, Part XII's "survival condition enacted by the environment" against Part IV's "No member of the history represents ... the survival condition". Check the patches: bit once - setting aside Part 0's blindness is a patch made in advance, and its bill arrives as the no-representation clause; the historical half had nothing to reach, since no earlier version of this draft exists in the record. Look inside: COULD NOT BITE. The sentence that leaves it nothing is section 10's "The grain is text. Org_l of a transformer is outside the programme by choice" together with section 11's "Anything at the grain of weights or activations". Every change the draft admits looks at what goes in and what comes out; the part it would have settled, M8's attention half, is left UNKNOWN. What the change list leaves out, said openly by the draft: the weights grain, the skill's own faults, the semantics itself, the other model. What it leaves out without saying: the boundary and continuity indices.

5. WHAT WOULD MAKE IT HARDER TO VARY. Declare Org_l at the grain of text, and beta and Omega, before M4, M5, M6, M8 and M9 use predicates that carry them - this one change moves four parts from "held if" towards held or cut. Split M8's two losses and re-anchor the partition claim to Part VI's critical block and interference, which would also stop P2.3 and P3.3 predicting opposite things about the same arm. Add the two left_out notions the draft's own predictions need: the finite monotone theorem with "No upward closure and no minimal member are assumed" (which is what makes P1.4's held and idle mean anything) and grain as a declared index.

6. WHAT THIS DOES NOT SHOW. Nothing here bears on whether the model is true, whether an LLM agent is or is not a selected transport, or whether the phases would work. The marks say what holds the draft's USE of file 10 now: a loose use may be a right one, and a held use may be false. Hard to vary is not truth. I tested a reading against a document's words, not a model against the world, and the parts I left unknown are unknown, not unneeded.

7. ONE NEXT STEP. Before phase 1 is written, settle the one clause the whole of M2 hangs on and which needs no run: whether any occurrence in a reader's selection history represents t, H or the survival condition.
